blocks.text: Another local chief, Kapura, proves false-hearted as well: he speaks of handing the Guru over and imagines reward from the Mughals, only to receive the Guru's curse in return. (4–6)
The betrayal of Kapura is later fulfilled in the poet's telling, while the Guru moves onward into the tract near Jaal Pilu and keeps gathering rough but loyal support. (7–9)
There, foreign coin and other supplies are distributed among Sikhs and Jat companions so the wandering force can remain mobile, armed, and ready in the forest zone. (10–12)
